clue.text: Baby first finds baby food, it's said, rather sharp

indicators.note: it's said tells us the letters built are to be heard rather than spelt as they stand

parts.note: the first letter of Baby, B, followed by RUSK, a hard biscuit given to teething infants

explanation.surface: A baby food that tastes rather sharp to an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: B (the first letter of 'Baby') plus RUSK sounds like the answer, whose spelling ends -QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brusque manners are curt and abrupt, a rather sharp way of speaking.

clue.text: The satisfaction of slaying great wolf

indicators.note: slaying the wolf tears it apart, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunter's glow of satisfaction after killing an enormous wolf.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterglow is the pleasant feeling of contentment that lingers after a success.

clue.text: I'm involved in slip-up in surveillance

indicators.note: being involved in something puts one piece inside the other
in a down clue, up means the word for slip is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a slip is a lapse, a small error
read as 'I am involved': the letter I is what goes inside

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to a slip-up while on a surveillance job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAPSE into ESPAL, and 'involved in' puts I inside it, after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is an old word for spying or watching, the act of observation.

clue.text: In air, creature heading to place where animals die

indicators.note: In places the following pieces inside the word for air

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heading here means going in front, so the creature comes before the word to

parts.note: a bat is a flying creature, fitting the air

explanation.surface: A bat flies through the air on its way to somewhere animals go to die.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is the place where livestock are killed for meat.

clue.text: G-men tackled Owen violently to get admission

indicators.note: the tackle is violent, so the letters of the three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: FBI agents bring down a man called Owen to extract a confession.
explanation.walkthrough: G-men are American FBI agents; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An acknowledgement is a confession or owning up, which is an admission.

clue.text: Detectives to return in temper and resign

indicators.note: in puts the detectives inside the word meaning temper

parts.note: to temper is to moderate or abate

indicators.note: to return means the detectives' letters go back the other way

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A detective's bad temper leads to a resignation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb meaning moderate; 'to return' turns CID into DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne or office, to step down.

clue.text: The first split in swing

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of The

parts.note: to rend is to tear or split apart

explanation.surface: The first crack appears in a swing on a playground.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a general shift in direction, as in a swing of opinion or fashion.

clue.text: European, I.e. Brian cross

indicators.note: cross here signals the letters are angrily mixed up, an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone notes that Brian is cross.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iberian comes from the peninsula of Spain and Portugal in Europe.

clue.text: Builds pontoons at head of channel

indicators.note: at says the letter from channel goes at the front
head of takes the leading letter of channel

parts.note: pontoons are floating platforms, rafts

explanation.surface: Engineers build pontoons at the start of a channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To craft is to make skilfully, to build by hand.

clue.text: Anchor on reef where female is missing her breakfast

parts.note: a kedge is a small anchor used for warping a ship

indicators.note: is missing says the female letter has been taken away from reef

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship anchored on a reef with the woman aboard missing her breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: REEF without F leaves REE; 'her' only links the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is a dish of rice, smoked fish and eggs traditionally eaten as a British breakfast.

clue.text: Iranian wounded ian's toes

indicators.note: wounded toes are damaged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the S of the possessive is needed as a letter here

explanation.surface: Ian's toes have been injured.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ossetian people and language of the Caucasus belong to the Iranian family.

clue.text: Rogue to fall for club assistant

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue
to fall in battle is to die

explanation.surface: A scoundrel falls for an assistant at the club.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's clubs, assisting on the course.

clue.text: Seal off a sub-standard building

parts.note: to bung up is to stop or seal off an opening
low means poor or below standard

explanation.surface: Inspectors seal off a shoddy building.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a single-storey house, a type of building.

clue.text: Plaintiff threw light on giant complex

parts.note: lit means illuminated, threw light on

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters of giant are mixed

explanation.surface: A plaintiff shed light on a giant complex of buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' looks like a noun but rearranges GIANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigant is a party to a lawsuit, such as one who brings the case.

clue.text: Arrive uninvited — wicket to fall

parts.note: a wicket is a small gate
to crash is to fall heavily

explanation.surface: Arriving uninvited at a cricket match just as a wicket falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, but 'wicket' here is its older sense, a small gate or door.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to attend a party or event without an invitation.

clue.text: Girdles once less elaborate

indicators.note: elaborate means intricately worked, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Girdles that were once less fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: To girdle is to encircle, as a belt goes around the waist.

clue.text: Bound to have hospital unit entertained

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
to wine and dine someone is to entertain them

explanation.surface: Staff of a hospital department are entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: Entwined means twisted together, bound up with one another.

clue.text: One in frenzied onrush for feed

indicators.note: in puts the letter for one inside the shuffled word
frenzied means wild and disordered, so the letters of onrush are mixed

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone in a frenzied rush for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frenzied' turns ONRUSH into NOURSH, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to give food and sustenance.

clue.text: Siamese king's governess tells stories, it's said, to count

indicators.note: it's said means the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: Anna Leonowens was governess to the King of Siam, and to tell stories is to tell lies

explanation.surface: The governess of the King of Siam tells stories to help him count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anna lies' spoken aloud gives the answer; Anna is the heroine of The King and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse figures is to tally and examine them, close to counting them up.

clue.text: Glen also built warlike 8

indicators.note: built means made up from parts, so the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: Glen also built warships.
explanation.walkthrough: The 8 points to the answer at 8 across, so the definition reads 'warlike vessels'.
explanation.definitionFit: Galleons were large sailing ships of the 16th century, often armed for war.

clue.text: Criminal nailer going straight

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A criminal nailer reforming and going straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going straight' looks like the reformed criminal but defines a straight line.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear means arranged in a line, so running straight.

clue.text: Blair is upset about universe ending

indicators.note: about means the shuffled name goes around the letter
upset means knocked over, so the letters of Blair are mixed

parts.note: U is an abbreviation for universal or universe

explanation.surface: Tony Blair is upset about the end of the universe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns BLAIR into BRIAL; 'about' puts it around U.
explanation.definitionFit: A burial is the final rite, the end of a life's story.

clue.text: Connected to digestive tract in part a mile across!

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A digestive tract measuring a mile across, to the setter's amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ileac means relating to the ileum, the last part of the small intestine.

clue.text: Bent marline spike originally made from non-organic material

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters of marline are rearranged
originally means at the start, taking the first letter of spike

explanation.surface: A bent marlinspike made from inorganic stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: A marlinespike is a sailor's tool for splicing rope; 'made from' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerals are naturally occurring inorganic substances such as ores and crystals.

clue.text: Landlord to tell fib about scene-shifting

indicators.note: about means the word for a fib goes around the other letters

parts.note: to tell a fib is to lie

indicators.note: shifting means moving about, so the letters of scene are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub landlord lies about moving the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landlord' suggests property, but here it is the keeper of a British pub; 'shifting' gives CENSE from 'scene'.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensee holds the licence to sell alcohol, so runs a British pub.

clue.text: Judge donkeys at Spithead

indicators.note: at places the letter from Spit at the end

parts.note: asses are donkeys

indicators.note: head takes the opening letter of Spit

explanation.surface: Judging donkeys at Spithead, an anchorage in the Solent off Portsmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Spithead is a stretch of water off Portsmouth; the word splits into 'Spit' and its 'head', the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or appraise, as a judge does.

clue.text: Strapping son found in wood

indicators.note: found in places the letter for son inside the wood

parts.note: a thicket is a dense growth of trees, a wood

explanation.surface: A strapping son discovered in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset means heavily built and sturdy, like a strapping person.
